scope: Claims supported or restricted by the inspected historical archive; no prospective outcomes.

claims.statement: In the completed MBPP final n=64 evaluation, Plain improves pass@1 while correct AST richness drops.
limits: AST richness is an implementation proxy.

claims.statement: Plain pass@64 falls from 0.720 to 0.704 despite pass@1 rising; the paired difference is -0.016 with 95% CI [-0.040, 0.008].
limits: This does not establish a causal effect of AST collapse or measured harm on each natural case.

claims.statement: SPECTRUM retains more correct AST richness than Plain and the projection control at the historical final n=64 checkpoint, while remaining below the initial model.
limits: Pass@1 noninferiority fails against both controls at the recorded absolute 0.01 margin.
Do not describe this as preserving all diversity or improving all endpoints.

claims.statement: The separate completed n=16 SSD continuation retains higher C16 and marginal D4 than SPECTRUM, while SPECTRUM has higher pass@1 and reported pass@16.
limits: Different eligible task sets for marginal D4.
No newly audited paired cross-run SSD comparison.
Do not substitute missing n=64 SSD results with its n=16 scores or pilot scores.

claims.statement: Correct AST richness alone does not establish retention of distinct semantic algorithms.
claims.required_evidence: Bounded blind annotation and audited natural programs, or retain an implementation-proxy-only claim.

claims.statement: The archive contains selected real-task AST contrasts, but not a completed audit showing the full natural iterative-collapse chain with consequence.
claims.required_evidence: Complete the documented natural-case gate with actual programs and labels; do not fill missing outcomes with illustrative inventions.

claims.statement: A projection comparison alone cannot isolate whether calibrated orientation, soft attenuation strength, reference information, or realized token budget explains the effect.
claims.required_evidence: Prespecified bounded geometry/strength controls and an anchor-information control if causal information-budget claims are retained.
limits: No test-set selection of the main strength.
No claim of necessity from an inconclusive comparison.

claims.statement: Five sequential rounds are one training trajectory, not five independent repeats; task bootstrap intervals do not establish training-run reproducibility.
claims.required_evidence: Run the frozen independent replications and report per-run results plus the prespecified aggregate.

claims.statement: Historical HumanEval+/APPS final transfers are completed, but their outcomes do not establish universal improvements.
limits: APPS SPECTRUM has lower pass@16 and C16 than Plain in point estimates.
No completed SSD transfer comparison was established by this audit.

claims.statement: The completed four-model by five-benchmark baseline matrix evaluates base models; it is not a completed trained-method matrix.
Do not claim the first iterative self-distillation method. The contribution must be scoped to this spectral generation intervention and its tested retention question.
Matched candidate counts and update schedules do not imply equal generated tokens, wall time, memory, or FLOPs.
claims.required_evidence: Report measured length and resource records for each arm; label missing resources explicitly.

minimal_remaining_work.item: Complete Natural Gate 0 using actual archived or prospectively collected programs, with transparent case selection and no invented per-case consequence.
Execute the frozen finite main study with Plain, SSD recipe adaptation and SPECTRUM, matched evaluation decoding and samples, retained checkpoints, and independent training replications.
Measure the intervention-generator and native-student stages on aligned tasks to separate generation effects from post-SFT retention.
Run the finite strength/loss/geometry diagnostics already in the approved study; require an anchor-only information control if retaining a claim that excludes reference-information advantage.
Complete fixed frozen transfer with all main comparators. Keep adapted benchmark protocols, failure counts, eligibility, and compute costs explicit.
Write the paper after the planned artifacts are complete, regardless of outcome. Do not add models, tasks, strengths or repeats to chase a favorable result.
